session-record.description: The current session stays primary, with requested work, scoped tabs and expandable child sessions.

states.rest: Requested work, findings and five children
states.question: A question without an invented task

judgment: Does the actual record preserve the approved order and compact hierarchy in both themes?
Do long Korean requests and missed rows remain legible in a narrow lane? Native behavior is verified separately.

pr-card.description: The approved PR card without duplicate agent action box, with real CI counts and labelled GitHub link.
judgment: Are the GitHub action, CI breakdown, timeline, files and body clear at narrow widths?
Native host, external GitHub writes and provider behavior require separate runtime evidence.

sidebar-task-lens.description: The sidebar's 프로젝트 | 태스크 switch and 태스크 list, the lane's 보기 slot holding a PR card or a session record, the rail Memory · PRs | Files · Changes and the PRs tool (PRD sidebar-task-lens D-50, the approved v4 boards).

states.rest: The 태스크 list by status at rest, the row of the pane with the keyboard selected.

judgment: The gallery scene draws the 태스크 list alone; the windows (A, C), the record in the 보기 slot (E) and the PRs tool (F) are compared against an isolated app capture, not a scene.
Do the groups, the second lines in the warning and danger colours, the child marks and the PR marks read as the boards draw them in both themes?
Are long Korean titles recognizable at 240 without hiding the PR mark or the time?

pane-header.description: The approved B2 pane header: identity and own PR on the first row, core state counts without a separate total or internal divider on the second-row overlay, compact counts beside an ask band.

states.rest: Core bands, child counts and representative lines, unknown and zero-child header identities.

judgment: B2 was approved from the interactive HTML comparison; this board records its layout in both themes using the existing tokens. Compare each state's production and native captures with the approved arrangement.

Does the ask band retain its request and Open action beside the compact ! count, with no separate total, internal divider or duplicate 외 N건 trigger? Does the request keep readable space at narrow widths and enlarged text?
Do the ancestor path, fork and own PR remain on the first row, with child counts on the second row and a core-ranked child line only when no core band takes that slot?

Are ordinary child requests distinct from operator-raised requests, unknown distinct from resting, and reported results distinct from verified task delivery? Does an empty parent lose the child row without changing the terminal grid?

projects-sidebar.description: The single sidebar: operator roots and orphans under projects and checkouts.

states.rest: No pointer on the list and no keyboard focus.
states.hover-parent: The pointer on the unfolded parent agent a1.
states.focus-parent: Keyboard focus on the unfolded parent agent a1.
states.checkout-closed: main's agent rows closed with its chevron, so its status badge counts them.

judgment: Each reference, current Pen and actual trio: do spacing, weight, color and alignment carry the same intent?
Every difference visible between Pen and the actual screen: acceptable renderer difference, or drift to fix in Pen or code?
Long Korean titles at the narrow width: is what the truncation keeps still recognizable?
Hover and focus captures: is the feedback visible enough without moving anything?

workspace-servers.description: Open server remains in the shared Workspace toolbar with the right lane closed; the picker distinguishes reachable IPv4/IPv6 endpoints without a redundant footer.

states.server-picker: Open server remains in the shared Workspace toolbar with the right lane closed; the picker distinguishes reachable IPv4/IPv6 endpoints without a redundant footer.

judgment: Open server remains in the shared Workspace toolbar with the right lane closed; the picker distinguishes reachable IPv4/IPv6 endpoints without a redundant footer.

area-focus.description: Keyboard ownership across two View areas using the shared Agent/View area renderer.

states.rest: First area owns the keyboard; each area retains its selected tab.

judgment: Does exactly one area read as the keyboard owner while the other selected tab remains recognizable?
Are Korean text and the native page content readable in the app, including narrow and expanded panels?
Does the foreground underline identify the keyboard area without a colored perimeter?

factory.description: The Factory screens: the 라인 with 결정 필요 on top (PRD factory-human-loop), the graph and the Task page, beside the shell's sidebar with the Factory row and the 비서 row.

states.line: 라인 at rest: 결정 필요 on top with its items open, one row per Task beneath, the person's turn in the warning band, 후속 후보 folded at the foot.
states.board: 보드: four lanes by movement, 시작 전 · 진행 중 · 멈춤 (나를 기다림, 다른 걸 기다림) · 완료, with the narrow lanes drawing their cards small and old completions folded.
states.graph: 그래프: layered Tasks with arrows, none for a dependency a longer path implies, and the unrelated Tasks below.
states.task: Task page of the verifying Task: the state sentence, the track with who decided where, summary, the criteria checklist, decisions split 나 / AI with one 다른 답 open, the activity timeline, the original issue and its 후속 후보.

judgment: The 라인 and Task page frames are the approved design of PRD factory-human-loop with no reference picture: do spacing, weight, color and alignment carry the same intent as the Pen frame? The graph keeps its reference picture e3.
The Dark frames are set against the Light ones. Does Dark use the tokens as the Light does, with the same hierarchy?
Does each 결정 필요 item read as one decision: the sentence, what stopped, the choices with their results and 추천, 다른 답, the default line, and the folded 근거?
Is the warning band on the person's rows the only colour that says whose turn it is, on the 라인, the board and the graph?
Long Korean titles and the long issue number: is a title still recognizable where the row cuts it, and does nothing overlap?

factory-board.description: The Factory board by movement and the one card at three sizes (PRD factory-board-cards): the board window, the graph with small cards, and every kind of card at the small, normal and wide widths.

states.board: 보드: four lanes by movement, 시작 전 · 진행 중 · 멈춤 (나를 기다림, 다른 걸 기다림) · 완료, with the narrow lanes drawing their cards small and old completions folded.
states.graph: 그래프: layered Tasks as small cards with arrows, none for a dependency a longer path implies, and the unrelated Tasks below.
states.sizes: 같은 카드, 세 크기: every kind of card (답 필요, 머지 대기, 멈춤, 실행 중, 하위 에이전트, 검증 중, 쉬는 중, 밖에서 진행, 시작 전, 완료) at 210, 300 and 470 px.

judgment: Does the eye land on the title, the one colored state icon, the problem line and the left band first, with everything else small and gray?

Does each size drop the less important parts first: small keeps the numbers, logo, icon and a two-line title; normal adds the summary, bar, problem and one button; wide adds the second summary line, the state word with the worker mark, the other buttons and the ✦ line?
Is 멈춤 the one lane to look at, with 나를 기다림 above 다른 걸 기다림, and do the narrow 시작 전 and 완료 lanes read as quiet?
Does the hatched current cell read as stopped at that stage without a word, in Light and Dark?
Long Korean titles and long English identifiers: does each size cut them at its line count without overlap, breaking Korean between words rather than inside one?

factory-observer.description: The Factory with Factory AI as Observer (PRD factory-observer): the settings in each mode, all projects, picking the worker, and the cards the Observer changes. Its 내 차례, paused and quiet Task page frames were replaced by the 라인 and Task page of the factory target (PRD factory-human-loop).

states.obs-set: 설정 · hide with 함께: the three mode cards, the table of who answers, Factory AI's agent and today's use, three worker candidates.
states.obs-direct: 설정 · 직접 with one candidate and 고급 설정 open.
states.obs-auto: 설정 · 맡김 with five candidates, today's AI use at 100/100.
states.obs-off: 설정 with Hide AI off: the modes dimmed with the note that every decision comes to the person.
states.obs-all: 설정 · 모든 프로젝트: one row per Factory with state, mode and worker, and the machine's worker total.
states.obs-pick: The Task page before it starts, with the worker menu open and Factory AI's pick marked.
states.obs-cards: The five cards the Observer changes (answer, wrong card, no report, worker gone, paused) at 210, 300 and 470 px.

judgment: Do the three mode cards and the table say who answers each kind of decision without reading a paragraph?
With Hide AI off or the day's use full, is it plain that every decision comes to the person?
On the worker pick, is Factory AI's pick and its reason one quiet line under what it explains?

core-move-devices.description: Settings > Devices with the core's badge and the move's entry, and the move dialog over Settings in its five forms (PRD core-host-node-move B2 to B5, D-06; the operator's flow B).

states.devices: This Mac runs the core: its row wears the core badge, Mac mini and build-box are SSH devices this core dials.
states.devices-menu: Mac mini's ⋯ menu open with core를 이 기기로 옮기기… between the helper items and 제거….
states.devices-offline: build-box is not connected: its ⋯ menu shows the move entry dimmed with 연결 안 됨.
states.node-menu: The core runs on Mac mini and this window is the MacBook's: this Mac's ⋯ menu offers 연결 정보…, core를 이 Mac으로 되돌리기… and Mac mini core와 연결 끊기…, and Mac mini's row wears the badge with its hint.
states.checks-failed: The dialog's checks found two things to fix, each with its one command or what to do, and 다시 점검.
states.confirm: Every check passed: what happens, that it can be undone, and Mac mini로 옮기기.
states.moving: The five steps with the current one running.
states.failed: The step that failed, that this Mac's core is unchanged, and Retry.
states.done: Moved: the phone's QR line and 되돌리기.
states.waiting: Amendment 4, drawn by analogy with the moving form (not in the approved bundle): Mac mini took the move's link and stopped answering; the steps, the waiting line and 그만 기다리기 as the footer's only action.
states.give-up: Amendment 4: the confirm of giving the wait up, as a state of the same dialog: that it cannot be undone, that this Mac's core starts again as it was, that a core coming back on Mac mini is set aside, the one plain risk line, and 그만 기다리기 as the destructive action beside 취소.
states.take-here: Amendment 4, the move back's counterpart from the MacBook's window: take the core here from the copy received, Mac mini's core held until it retires, no risk line, and 여기로 가져오기 beside 취소.
states.abandoned: Amendment 4: the wait was given up; this Mac's core runs as it was and Mac mini's core stops once this Mac reaches it, with 닫기.

judgment: Is the core badge on This Mac quiet beside the name, and does the move's entry sit in the ⋯ menu where the bundle puts it?
Does each dialog form name the reason first and keep one primary action?
Korean particles after the machine's name (로/으로, 는/은): do they read as Korean reads the name?
The Dark frames are set against the Light ones: does Dark use the tokens as Light does?

The give-up and take-here confirms have no approved frame: do they read as the move dialog's own confirm, with the line that it cannot be undone first, the risk line in the body color like the lines above it, and the destructive action not the default?

core-move-window.description: A window whose core runs on another machine: the rail with the core machine's crown (N1) and the strip that names the move, the core's update, an unreachable core and a link the operator ended (PRD core-host-node-move B2, W1 to W3, B10, B16).

states.rail-node: The MacBook's window, core on Mac mini: This Mac first with the laptop glyph, then Mac mini with the crown in its bottom-left corner and a Needs You mark, then build-box not connected.
states.rail-core: Mac mini's own window: This Mac first wearing the crown, then the MacBook that dials in.
states.window-moving: W1: the strip names the move's step of five while the window takes no input.
states.window-updating: W2: the strip says the core is being updated to this app's build and agents keep running.
states.window-unreachable: W3: the strip says the core cannot be reached and the window reconnects.
states.window-disconnected: B16, drawn by analogy with W3 (not in the approved bundle): the operator ended the link here and the strip offers 다시 연결.
states.window-waiting: Amendment 4, drawn by analogy with W1 (not in the approved bundle): the move waits on Mac mini, and the strip offers 그만 기다리기, which only opens the move dialog at its confirm.

judgment: Is the crown readable at 9 px in the tile's bottom-left notch without fighting the Needs You mark or the ×?
Does each strip state read in one line in the badge's place, with … for waiting and ! for a problem?
The disconnected strip has no approved frame: does it read as the same family as W3, with 다시 연결 as the only action?
The waiting strip has no approved frame: does 그만 기다리기 sit as the strip's one action, the same family as 다시 연결?

first-run-onboarding.description: The first run (PRD first-run-onboarding D-20, D-27): the three-step wizard over the dimmed shell in every state its steps carry, the start panel it closes into, the empty Home with Add project on the Projects label, and Settings > Notifications on each system.

states.agents-changes: Step 1 with What changes open: one row per path with the agents that share it, then the hide command (board 02).
states.agents-failed: Step 1 after Continue failed for Codex: the reason line and Try again (board 02, B12).
states.agents-none: Step 1 with no agent installed: one line and two install links (board 02, B9).
states.agents-setup: Step 1 reopened from Help > Set up Hide, with its close button (board 02, B46).
states.agents-windows: Step 1 on Windows: OpenCode and Cursor read Not on Windows yet, Continue reads Ctrl+Enter (board 15).
states.notifications: Step 2 on macOS before anything is pressed (board 03).
states.notifications-blocked: Step 2 while macOS blocks Hide (board 03, B15).
states.notifications-unreadable: Step 2 when the setting cannot be read (board 03, B17).
states.notifications-no-service: Step 2 on Linux with no notification service (board 12, B48).
states.start-panel: The start panel the wizard closes into, on a signed-in agent (board 05).
states.start-panel-signed-out: The start panel on an agent that is not signed in (board 05, B23).
states.home-no-project: Empty Home with no project, and the + on the Projects label (boards 06, 17).
states.home-no-agent: Empty Home with a project and no agent (board 06).
states.home-no-project-windows: Empty Home on Windows, with its shortcut labels (board 14).
states.settings-on: Settings > Notifications with notifications on and allowed (board 07).
states.settings-blocked: Settings > Notifications while macOS blocks Hide (board 07).
states.settings-on-windows: Settings > Notifications on Windows with the Test notification row (board 13).

judgment: Each board draws several states at once and the bundle pairs it with the scene at rest; the state sheets hold every state the scene draws. Do the built steps, the start panel, the empty Home and the Settings rows carry the spacing, weight, color and alignment of their boards in both themes?
The startup and failure screen (board 09) and the Factory line (board 08) are not on this scene; they are checked against their boards from the desktop app and the Factory scene.

Filters and summary wrap at narrow widths; horizontal scrolling stays within the table.
The popover switches between seven daily bars and thirty small contribution squares, with matching totals, daily hover, keyboard preview and click-to-pin.

Do the tab lines (the manual name, and Tab 3 for the unnamed tab) read as quiet heads inside the guide, their glyph on the status-mark column and their name on the title column, and do neutral selection, Korean titles and trailing metadata match the approved Pen in both themes?

right-lane.description: The right lane (PRD right-lane, sidebar-task-lens): Agent Views fill the body and one lane of four tools (Memory, PRs, Files, Changes) opens from the rail, over the agents or pinned beside them, with the file tree as its own column.

states.overlay: Files over the agents, unpinned; the terminals keep their width.
states.pinned: Files pinned and docked beside the agents behind the divider.
states.tree-overlay: The tree on beside the document, over the agents; the lane widens by the tree.

states.expanded: The lane expanded over the whole body, tree on.
states.prs: PRs pinned, its header naming the project scope and the rail carrying the PRs tool's Needs You count.
states.narrow: A 1040 px window: the pinned lane opens over the agents, the pin still on.

judgment: Does the lane read as one surface over or beside the agents, its rail, header, pin, tree button and divider matching the boards?
Does opening over the agents keep the terminals at their width, with only pinning narrowing them, once?

view-opener-feedback.description: View opener mark and View feedback (PRD view-opener-feedback D-20, D-24, D-25): the opener's logo on a View tab, the pane header's N views, Comment mode on pages, diffs, files, images and PDFs, the feedback row with Send and its menu, and what follows Send.

states.opener-tip: A View tab's opener mark with its tooltip above the tab, unsent counts on the tabs (board 1).
states.views-list: The pane header's `2 views` list open (board 2).
states.comment-browser: Comment mode on a page: the hint, an outlined element, numbered pins and a region (board 3).
states.comment-diff: A diff with a range note being written and a commented line with its bar and note (board 4).
states.comment-pdf: A PDF in Comment mode with an area note naming its page (board 5).
states.send-menu: The ▾ Send menu open over the feedback row, agent logos hidden (board 6).
states.sent: After Send: `Sent 3 to <name> · delivered when it rests` with Go to pane (board 7).

judgment: Does the 10 px opener mark sit on the kind icon's lower right, keep the kind readable, and open its tooltip above the tab, in both themes?
Do pins and image/PDF regions show only while Comment is on, with the tab count and the feedback row carrying the comments otherwise?
Do the feedback row, the Send button (always with its logo) and the ▾ menu (status mark and name; the logo only while the agent logo view mode shows it) match board 6?

Each window is paired with one state; the state cells under it on its board (boards vof-<board>-l/d in the bundle's .pen) carry the rest, including Not delivered, Couldn't send and `Comment deleted · Undo`, and are judged in the state sheets.
